entities.summary: Sofia is the capital and largest city of Bulgaria, situated in the Sofia Valley at the foot of the Vitosha mountain in the western part of the country. The city has a humid continental climate and is built west of the Iskar river, with many mineral springs, such as the Sofia Central Mineral Baths. Founded in the 7th century BC by the Thracians, Sofia played a significant role in the Roman Empire and was an important center of trade and commerce. The city was later influenced by the Byzantine Empire and Ottoman Empire, before becoming the capital of modern Bulgaria in 1878. Sofia's rich history is evident in its many historical landmarks, including the Alexander Nevsky Cathedral and the National Historical Museum. The city's cultural scene is thriving, with numerous museums, galleries, and festivals throughout the year. Sofia is a popular tourist destination, attracting visitors from around the world with its unique blend of history, culture, and natural beauty.
